$comment: Typecheck program for scripts/__tests__/** — the test code that guards the
build pipeline itself (resolve-drivers, resolve-pro, pack-ep, sign-ep,
driver stash, CI scripts). Until this existed, no file under scripts/ was in
ANY tsc program: the root tsconfig include list is src + packages/*, so
'tsc --noEmit is clean' covered 0% of these files.
allowJs is REQUIRED, not a relaxation. The tests import the build scripts as
`.mjs`; with allowJs off, every one of those imports fails with TS7016
'implicitly has an any type', which silently voids the type of everything the
scripts export (measured: 33 TS7016 + 44 downstream implicit-any errors).
A gate that cannot see the module under test is not a gate.
checkJs stays OFF. Turning it on type-checks the build scripts themselves and
yields 343 errors across the .mjs files reachable from these tests (472 across
all of scripts/), almost all missing JSDoc on a codebase that predates the
gate. That is a real backlog, not something to force green here — see
tsconfig.scripts-checkjs.json for the measurable version of it. The two counts
are themselves stale and are registered as a finding; measure with `npx tsc -p
tsconfig.scripts-checkjs.json --noEmit` rather than trusting the numbers here.
For the one file that IS enforced today see tsconfig.pack-ep.json.
scripts/e2e-screenshots/ is excluded on purpose, and it is NOT covered
elsewhere: editor-blog-screenshots.ts is a WebdriverIO spec that imports
@wdio/globals and e2e/helpers.ts, and e2e/tsconfig.json is the only config
declaring the @wdio types — but its `include` is ["**/*.ts"], which resolves
relative to e2e/ and therefore cannot reach scripts/. Measured with `tsc -p
<config> --noEmit --listFiles` across all five configs in this repo (root,
scripts, scripts-checkjs, pack-ep, e2e): the file is in ZERO programs. An
earlier version of this comment claimed it "belongs to the e2e/tsconfig.json
program"; that was false. Excluding it here keeps the status quo honest
rather than half-fixing it — putting it in a real program is registered as a
finding, not done silently.
